checks.title: Tailscale is logged in and Running when installed
checks.rationale: A node that dropped to NeedsLogin or Stopped (or whose tailscaled is not running) has no tailscale0 traffic: every firewall rule scoped to tailscale0 or 100.64.0.0/10 silently matches nothing, while everyone still believes SSH and the panel are private. Closing public SSH on such a host locks you out.
checks.fix: tailscale up (log the node in again), then prove SSH over the tailnet from a new session before relying on any tailnet only rule
checks.breaks: Nothing; logging in restores the tailnet paths the firewall already expects.

checks.title: Node key expiry is disabled on server nodes
checks.rationale: Tailscale node keys expire (180 days by default). When a server's key expires the node logs out on its own, usually unattended, and every tailnet scoped rule turns dead (see TS-001). Servers should have key expiry disabled in the admin console.
checks.fix: Disable key expiry for this machine in the Tailscale admin console (Machines, the node, Disable key expiry)
checks.breaks: Nothing on the host; a stolen node key then stays valid until you remove the node, so protect the host itself.

checks.title: Tailscale Funnel and Serve expose only what is intended
checks.rationale: Funnel publishes a local service to the whole internet through Tailscale's relays, bypassing the host firewall and any tunnel WAF. Serve publishes it to the tailnet. Both are easy to leave behind after a test, and neither shows up in ss or the firewall rules.
checks.verify: tailscale funnel status; tailscale serve status
checks.fix: tailscale funnel reset (and tailscale serve reset) if the exposure is not intended
checks.breaks: Whatever was reached through the funnel or serve URL stops answering.

checks.title: Firewall rules that mention tailscale0 have a running tailnet behind them
checks.rationale: UFW rules on tailscale0 only work while Tailscale is installed, logged in and Running. Without it they are dead rules: they look like a private path in reviews and give none.
checks.verify: sudo ufw status verbose | grep tailscale0; tailscale status
checks.fix: Install and log in Tailscale, or remove the tailscale0 rules and keep a path you actually have
checks.breaks: Removing the rules is harmless when Tailscale is gone; check you still have another way in first.

checks.title: Tailnet Lock state
checks.rationale: Tailnet Lock makes nodes verify new node keys with signing keys you hold, so a compromised coordination server cannot add nodes to your tailnet. It is optional and adds key management; this check only reports whether it is on.
checks.fix: Consider Tailnet Lock for tailnets that reach servers (tailscale lock init)
